pilot: P3c generalisation lane 8 — CIE 9709 Pure 1 subtopic 1.8 Integration (operator order: next lane per INTEGRATION-PLAN)
modeNote: modesRecorded reflects the cross-map's mode flags of record: [1] facts, plus [4] where the resource is a pattern/doctrine exemplar (the primary picks). Mode-2 (deep-link rendering on lane pages) was dropped by operator directive 2026-10-22 and is not used.

1.8.1.officialText: understand integration as the reverse process of differentiation, and integrate ( ax + b ) (for any rational n except –1), together with constant multiples, sums and differences
1.8.1.spineTitleVerbatim: understand integration as the reverse process of differentiation, and integrate ( ax + b ) (for any rational n except –1), together with constant multiples, sums and differences

resources.title: What happens if we integrate, then differentiate?
resources.evidence: dI/da for I(a) = integral over [0,a] of (4-2^(x^2)) resolved by the integration-differentiation inverse relation — the reverse-process understanding of 1.8.1 clause one is the tested skill

resources.title: Can we find $\int 1/(\sqrt{x+2} - \sqrt{x+1}) dx$?
resources.evidence: part (i) rationalises 1/(sqrt(x+2)-sqrt(x+1)) into sqrt(x+2)+sqrt(x+1) and integrates the (x+c)^(1/2) terms — canonical (ax+b)^n antiderivatives; the surrounding parts (trig substitution, partial fractions) are P3-dressed and the lane-6 routing named 1.8 Integration as the home
resources.examProvenance: UCLES A level Mathematics B Special paper, QP 9202/0, 1981, Q3

1.8.2.officialText: solve problems involving the evaluation of a constant of integration
1.8.2.spineTitleVerbatim: solve problems involving the evaluation of a constant of integration
1.8.2.ugmStation: Calculus Meets Functions + Calculus of Powers + Product Rule

resources.title: Can we find a curve from its gradient function?
resources.evidence: integrates dy/dx = 4x-3 to y = 2x^2-3x+c and evaluates c from the minimum value -1/8 — the constant-of-integration step is 1.8.2 load-bearing
resources.examProvenance: UCLES O level Additional Mathematics 2, QP 471/2, 1968, Q3

resources.title: If $dy/dx$ is inversely proportional to $x^2$, can we find $y$?
resources.evidence: part (ii) integrates dy/dx = 4/x^2 to y = -4/x + d and evaluates d from y(2)=1 — reverse-process integration of x^(-2) with constant-of-integration evaluation; part (i) is product-rule turning-point work (1.7.4-dressed)
resources.examProvenance: UCLES O level Additional Mathematics 1, QP 471/1, 1969, Q4

resources.title: Given three clues, can we find the equation of the curve?
resources.evidence: gradient ax+b integrated to y = ax^2/2+bx+c with c evaluated from a point — the constant-of-integration reconstruction is the decisive step
resources.examProvenance: Cambridge Assessment Group Archives. The question remains Copyright University of Cambridge Local Examinations Syndicate (“UCLES”),

resources.title: Thinking constantly
resources.evidence: displacement recovered from velocity by integration with initial-condition constants — reverse-process integration plus constant-of-integration evaluation (mechanics context is a wrapper; the lane-7 routing recorded the 1.8 bearing)

1.8.3.ugmStation: Calculus Meets Functions + Calculus of Powers + Chain Rule

resources.title: Additional integrals
resources.evidence: given definite integrals of f and g over [0,3], evaluate linear combinations, reversed limits and shifted-argument integrals — linearity and order-reversal properties of the definite integral are the tested skill

resources.title: Integral chasing
resources.evidence: four chained definite integrals of 10x+3, b*sqrt(x)+a/sqrt(x), 1/x^5-1/x^2 and x^(b/a)(sqrt(x)-1/sqrt(x)) plus an area check — power-rule integration with fractional and negative indices is the tested skill

resources.title: What does it mean if a function $f(x)=f(2\alpha-x)$?
resources.evidence: bilateral-function question proves the order-reversal identity for polynomial definite integrals and reasons about G(t) as a signed area — polynomial definite integration is load-bearing (extension-style framing)

resources.title: If we know $f(x)$, can we find $\int_{-1}^1 f(x^2-1) \:dx$?
resources.evidence: evaluates a definite integral of a piecewise-linear f composed with x^2-1 by reducing to the integral of x^2 over [-1,1] — definite integration of x^2 after composition

resources.title: Can we find the area under a parabola?
resources.evidence: I(c) = integral over [0,1] of ((x-c)^2+c^2) expanded, integrated and minimised by completing the square — canonical polynomial definite integral

resources.title: When does this definite integral have a minimum?
resources.evidence: I(a) = integral over [0,1] of (x^2-a)^2 evaluated and minimised — polynomial definite integral

resources.title: If $f(x)$ always satisfies this equation, what is $\int_{-1}^1 f(x)\: dx$?
resources.evidence: functional-equation multiple choice resolved by integrating a polynomial identity over [-1,1] with the definite integral as an unknown constant

resources.title: Slippery areas
resources.evidence: definite-integral values recovered from area data under transformations, with the sqrt(x+5) evaluation reducing to an (x+5)^(3/2) antiderivative — (ax+b)^n technique inside definite-interval evaluation (the lane-7 routing recorded the 1.8 bearing)

resources.title: Stretch the function
resources.evidence: scaling functions to satisfy an integral-equals-1 condition over [-1,2] — linearity, signed value and definite evaluation incl. x^(1/2) and x^(-2) (rational n != -1)

resources.title: What else do you know?
resources.evidence: from an area datum, evaluates definite integrals of f+5, f(x+2) and -f over shifted intervals — linearity and translation properties of the definite integral (the lane-7 routing recorded the 1.8 bearing)

1.8.4.officialText: use definite integration to find lines parallel to the axes, or between a curve and a line or between two curves: • the area of a region bounded by a curve and • a volume of revolution about one of the axes.
1.8.4.spineTitleVerbatim: use definite integration to find lines parallel to the axes, or between a curve and a line or between two curves: • the area of a region bounded by a curve and • a volume of revolution about one of the axes.
1.8.4.ugmStation: Calculus Meets Functions + Calculus of Powers

resources.title: Meaningful areas
resources.evidence: areas of the regions enclosed by sqrt(x), x^2, x, (x^2+x)/2 and 2*sqrt(x)-x — area between curves by definite integration

resources.title: What volume is generated when $y = ax - x^2$ is rotated about the x-axis?
resources.evidence: the area under ax-x^2 given as 36 finds a, then the solid of revolution about the x-axis is evaluated as pi*integral((6x-x^2)^2)dx — the canonical P1 area-then-volume-of-revolution question
resources.examProvenance: Cambridge Assessment Group Archives. The question remains Copyright University of Cambridge Local Examinations Syndicate (“UCLES”),

resources.title: Can we find the centre of mass of a solid hemisphere?
resources.evidence: volume of revolution of y = b(a^2-x^2)^(1/2)/a about the x-axis evaluated as a polynomial integral; the centre-of-mass parts are Mechanics dressing
resources.examProvenance: UCLES A level Mathematics A 2, QP 840/2, 1973, Q17

resources.title: Can we sketch the graph of $y^2 = x^3$?
resources.evidence: area enclosed by y^2 = x^3 and x = 4 evaluated as 2*integral(x^(3/2))dx and the volume of revolution as pi*integral(x^3)dx — rational-index powers rotated about an axis
resources.examProvenance: UCLES O level Additional Mathematics 1, QP 471/1, 1968, Q4

resources.title: What's the area enclosed by $y=x(x-3)^2$ and a tangent?
resources.evidence: part (b) area between the cubic and the tangent/chord PQ as a definite integral of curve minus line — the tangent-revisit area carries the recorded 1.8 bearing
resources.examProvenance: UCLES A level Mathematics 1, QP 186, 1951, Q9

resources.title: Can we find the area inside a straight line, a parabola and the x-axis?
resources.evidence: area of the region bounded by y = x^2, 2x+y=15 and the x-axis split into an integrated region and a triangle
resources.examProvenance: UCLES O level Additional Mathematics 1, QP 471/1, 1977, Q3

resources.title: If we take a slice from this sphere, where is its centre of gravity?
resources.evidence: volume of a spherical cap as pi*integral(a^2-x^2)dx; the centre-of-gravity parts are Mechanics dressing
resources.examProvenance: Cambridge Assessment Group Archives. The question remains Copyright University of Cambridge Local Examinations Syndicate (“UCLES”),

resources.title: When does a cubic curve have two turning points?
resources.evidence: part (iv) area enclosed by the x-axis and the translated cubic g(x) = x^2(x-t) — polynomial definite integration is the load-bearing step

resources.title: What's the area between $f_k(x) = x(x-k)(x-2)$ and the $x$-axis?
resources.evidence: area between a cubic and the x-axis written as a difference of two definite integrals with the sign split at the interior root — area-as-signed-integrals is the tested 1.8.4 skill

resources.title: When is the area of this region bigger than the area of this one?
resources.evidence: compares the areas bounded by the x-axis and a-x^2 vs x^4-a via definite integrals with irrational limits

resources.title: Can we find the area enclosed by this quadratic and the $x$-axis?
resources.evidence: area between y = 2x^2-6x+4 and the x-axis after gradient-condition reconstruction — the area computation carries the recorded 1.8 bearing
resources.examProvenance: UCLES O level Additional Mathematics 2, QP 420/2, 1963, Q4

resources.title: Can we find the area between a parabola and a line?
resources.evidence: area between y = x^2 and y = x+2 as the difference of two definite integrals — the canonical curve-line area question

coverage.coverageNote: Strand-lane semantics (lane-4 shape, applied to a spec section with no dedicated UGM station): UGM's two dedicated calculus stations are fully of record via lane 7 (Introducing Calculus 27/27, Calculus of Powers 48/48), so the 1.8 new-text universe is the 10 unrecorded resources of the wider seven-station calculus family whose tested skill is 1.8.x — all 10 ship mapped under pure-1-integration/ and none ship unmapped. The 18 further 1.8 rows are cross-lane fact joins to already-of-record bodies under pure-1-differentiation/ (13 flip the lane-7 Calculus-of-Powers non-overlaps of record — the integration-dressed honesty lane 7 deferred to this lane; 5 add one-to-many rows alongside standing 1.7 alignments; text untouched either way). 32 further candidates are routed to recorded homes (P3-integration technique pools, P3/Mechanics, trapezium-rule resources with no spine home, marker false positives, teacher-support pages) and recorded in sweepRouting — never forced (AGENT.md rule 3). Full-fidelity picture: 91 sweep candidates = 28 aligned (10 new-text + 18 cross-lane joins; 28 alignment rows) + 32 routed + 31 rejected with reasons.
